eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from the Pakistan Meteorological Department and global ensembles points to above-normal temperatures across Sindh during the second week of June, driven by an anticyclone promoting clear skies and limited moisture influx from the Arabian Sea. This setup favors peak readings near 38–41°C on June 11, with coastal humidity and sea-breeze effects creating narrow uncertainty bands around the daily maximum. Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 40–41°C outcomes because ensemble spreads show modest day-to-day variability in the timing of peak heating, while historical June extremes in Karachi rarely exceed 42°C without stronger pre-monsoon signals.
